traceability.evidence: Story file exists: docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md (verified by check_file_exists).,Rule implementation present: src/rules/require-branch-annotation.ts defines the ESLint rule `require-branch-annotation` with meta.docs.description "Require @story and @req annotations on code branches" and is annotated with @story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and @req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE.,Core branch detection and configurable scope: require-branch-annotation.ts uses validateBranchTypes(context) to determine branch types, then registers a handler for each branch type that calls reportMissingAnnotations(context, node, storyFixCountRef). DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES in src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts includes IfStatement, SwitchCase, TryStatement, CatchClause, ForStatement, ForOfStatement, ForInStatement, WhileStatement, DoWhileStatement and is annotated with REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA.,Comment association for branches: src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts exports gatherBranchCommentText, which for SwitchCase scans preceding comment lines; for other nodes uses sourceCode.getCommentsBefore; for CatchClause it also inspects comments inside the catch body (including a getCommentsInside-based strategy and a line-based fallback); for IfStatement it delegates to gatherElseIfCommentText to handle else-if positions. These helpers are annotated with @supports docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION.,Alternative @supports format support: getBranchAnnotationInfo in src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts parses branch comment text using regex; it treats any comment containing @supports as satisfying both story and req requirements: `const hasSupports = /@supports\b/.test(text); const missingStory = !/@story\b/.test(text) && !hasSupports; const missingReq = !/@req\b/.test(text) && !hasSupports;`. This directly implements REQ-SUPPORTS-ALTERNATIVE.,Annotation parsing and reporting: reportMissingAnnotations (src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts) uses getBranchAnnotationInfo to compute missingStory/missingReq, then calls reportMissingStory and reportMissingReq. These functions insert default `// @story .story.md` and `// @req ` comments via fixer.insertTextBeforeRange while reporting ESLint diagnostics with messageId 'missingAnnotation' and data.missing set to '@story' or '@req'. These functions are annotated with REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING.,Else-if and catch placement integration: branch-annotation-helpers.ts contains specialized logic for CatchClause (gatherCatchClauseCommentText) and else-if branches (gatherElseIfCommentText plus scanElseIfPrecedingComments, scanElseIfBetweenConditionAndBody, scanElseIfInsideBlockComments). This supports comments before catch, inside catch body, before else-if, between condition and block, and inside the consequent block, aligning with formatter behaviors (e.g., Prettier).,Configurable scope and invalid configuration handling: validateBranchTypes (branch-annotation-helpers.ts) checks context.options[0].branchTypes; if provided, it filters out invalid types (not in DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES). On invalid values, it returns a Program listener that reports `Value "" should be equal to one of the allowed values: ...` for each invalid type; otherwise it returns either the configured list or the default list. This matches REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE and the story’s invalid-configuration behavior.,User-facing error message: require-branch-annotation.ts defines meta.messages.missingAnnotation = "Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}.", so diagnostics clearly indicate which kind of annotation ('@story' or '@req') is missing. Tests assert messageId 'missingAnnotation' and the data.missing field (tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts via makeMissingAnnotationErrors).,Unit tests for rule behavior: tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts exercises the rule extensively. Valid cases include all significant branches with proper annotations: if, for, while, do-while, for-of, for-in, switch cases, try/finally, try/catch, nested ifs, default case without annotations (allowed), branchTypes configuration ignoring unlisted types, and branches annotated solely with @supports (REQ-SUPPORTS-ALTERNATIVE). Invalid cases cover missing annotations on all supported branch types, nested branches missing inner annotations, configurable branchTypes enforcing only specified types, Prettier-style else-if branch behavior, and invalid branchTypes configuration. The file header explicitly links to this story and requirements via @story and @supports annotations.,Performance test for large files: tests/perf/require-branch-annotation-large-file.test.ts builds a large source file with many nested branches (buildLargeNestedBranchSource with 200 functions and nestingDepth 3) and uses eslint.Linter with the rule. The rule's documentation also cites tests/integration/else-if-annotation-prettier.integration.test.ts as covering else-if + Prettier integration, demonstrating usage with real-world formatting scenarios.,Documentation for the rule: docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md documents the rule, referencing this story and requirements (REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE). traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and listed requirements for story 004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS are fully implemented and verified:
- Core functionality: The `require-branch-annotation` ESLint rule is implemented in src/rules/require-branch-annotation.ts. It uses DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES defined in src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts to cover all significant branches (if/else, try/catch, switch cases, and various loops). tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts contains comprehensive valid/invalid cases for all these branch types, and the jest run shows this suite passing. - Alternative format support: getBranchAnnotationInfo treats any comment containing @supports as satisfying both @story and @req, so branches annotated only with @supports are not reported as missing annotations. This is explicitly tested by three valid cases in tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts (if, try/catch, and else-if branches with only @supports), and the test suite passes. - Quality standards and performance: The rule uses standard ESLint RuleModule shape, meta.docs, messages, and schema, and delegates complexity to well-structured helpers. Performance is explicitly validated in tests/perf/require-branch-annotation-large-file.test.ts using eslint.Linter on a large, nested-branch synthetic file, asserting completion within 5 seconds. All tests pass, confirming acceptable performance. - Integration and complex structures: The helper functions in src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts handle complex branch patterns including nested branches and formatter-driven restructuring. There is special handling for CatchClause (supporting comments before and inside the block) and for else-if branches (comments before the else-if line, between condition and block, or inside the block). Utility tests and integration tests (e.g., catch-annotation-prettier.integration.test.ts) validate this behavior. - User experience and error handling: Diagnostics use messageId 'missingAnnotation' with message "Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}.", making it clear whether '@story' or '@req' is missing. For configuration errors, validateBranchTypes reports a specific message listing allowed branchTypes, and tests assert this behavior. Edge cases such as invalid branchTypes, default cases without annotations, nested branches, and multiple missing annotations are covered by tests. - Documentation: docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md provides user-facing documentation, including description, detailed behavior (especially for catch and else-if), configuration options, and examples of correct usage, incorrect code, and invalid configuration matching the implemented rule.
Given the presence of the rule, its helpers, comprehensive unit/integration/performance tests, clear error messages, configuration validation, and dedicated documentation, and with all relevant tests passing under `npm test`, this story is fully implemented and passes its acceptance criteria.
